newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency settles case against UCB unit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency settles case against UCB unit.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said on Tuesday it entered a settlement with UCB Chemicals Corp, UCB SA's U.S. subsidiary in Smyrna, Ga., for allegedly marking fungicides without proper labeling.
EPA and the California Department of Pesticide Regulation collectively negotiated a settlement for UCB to pay a civil penalty of $304,725, the agency said.

EPA alleged in a complaint that UCB marketed 40-pound boxes of its Ziram Granuflo fungicide in California that lacked approved labels with directions for use and worker protection standards, the agency said.
UCB spokesman Michael Toomey said the company worked to remedy the labeling problem as soon as it was identified in April 1995.
